notes: **Isotopes:** protium ($^1_1H$), deuterium ($^2_1H$ or D), tritium ($^3_1H$ or T). Tritium is radioactive with half-life 12.3 years.
**Atomic hydrogen:** produced by passing $H_2$ through an electric arc. Highly reactive and recombines to atomic form on cooling, releasing 436 kJ/mol.
**Nascent hydrogen:** hydrogen produced in situ during a chemical reaction. It is more reactive than ordinary molecular hydrogen because it is in an activated atomic state.
**Heavy water ($D_2O$):** used as moderator in nuclear reactors because it slows neutrons effectively without absorbing them. Also used in isotopic tracer studies.
**Hydrogen as fuel:** combustion $2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O$ releases 286 kJ/mol. Zero carbon emissions, but storage and transport are challenging because of low density and high reactivity.
